finding.claim: Unauthenticated path traversal in download(): the attacker-supplied query parameter 'f' is joined onto /srv/files with filepath.Join and read with os.ReadFile, with no containment check, so '../' sequences (including percent-encoded) escape the root and return arbitrary readable files.
finding.sink: files.go:13 os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)); contents written to response at files.go:18

trace.note: Attacker-controlled value 'f' read from the request query string, decoded by Query()
filepath.Join("/srv/files", name) cleans the path; f=../../etc/passwd resolves to /etc/passwd, outside root
File contents written directly to the HTTP response
download registered on default mux at /dl with no auth middleware

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, Clean-then-prefix check, filepath.Rel containment, or EvalSymlinks/realpath check between the join and the read; Join does not confine the result to root. No authentication or authorization on the handler or mux registration (files.go:32-34). Avatar handler (files.go:21-28) is NOT reported: filepath.Base at line 22 strips directory components, and u=.. resolves to a directory whose ReadFile errors, so no disclosure.

verdict.guard_found: none. Between the query read (files.go:12) and the read (files.go:13) there is no filepath.Base, prefix check, filepath.Rel, or symlink resolution. filepath.Join only cleans the path, so "../" sequences escape /srv/files. Query() percent-decodes, so encoded traversal also works. The handler is registered without auth on the default mux (files.go:32). The avatar handler's filepath.Base (files.go:22) does not apply to download().
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: files.go:12 takes the attacker's "f" value, files.go:13 joins it onto root with no containment check and reads the result with os.ReadFile, files.go:18 returns the bytes, and files.go:32 exposes /dl to anonymous callers, so an unauthenticated request for f=../../etc/passwd returns /etc/passwd.
